commonMistakes: Leaning away from the weights or shrugging excessively
Shuffling with tiny rushed steps instead of controlled strides
Holding your breath for the whole carry
cues: Walk like you're balancing a book on your head
instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand and stand tall.
Pull your shoulders slightly back and down, brace your core as if for a light punch.
Walk with short, controlled steps, keeping your torso upright — no leaning or swaying.
Set the weights down with control by hinging at the hips. Rest, then repeat.
longevityNotes: Carrying heavy things is a fundamental human movement — groceries, luggage, grandchildren. The farmer carry trains grip, posture, and core stability all at once, and it's self-regulating: your grip gives out long before anything dangerous happens. Walk 30-60 seconds per set, 2-3 times a week; your future self carrying groceries will thank you.
name: Farmer Carry

progression.loadingGuidance: Increase weight when you can carry for 60 seconds with perfect posture at RPE 7 or less.
progression.progressTo: Trap-bar carry or heavier dumbbells for distance
progression.regressTo: Single-arm suitcase carry with a light weight

safetyNotes: Clear your walking path first. If you have lower-back issues, start light and keep carries short; stop if you feel the need to lean sideways to compensate.
